title: Comparison of geometric module stalks normalized on constant sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\prime\to X$ have the same image point, where $\Omega,\Omega\prime$ are separably closed fields. On the category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], there exists a natural isomorphism $\beta:(-)_{s}\simeq(-)_{t}$ between the stalk functors [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For every $\Lambda$-module $M$, the component $\beta_{M_X}$ is identity on $M$ under the canonical identifications of the stalks of the constant sheaf $M_X$ [def-constructible-constant] with $M$. No monomorphism, subsheaf, genericity or finiteness is assumed.

proof.text: Use SpecToEquivOfField to express both geometric points by their common image x and residue-field embeddings. Choose the actual field SeparableClosure of kappa(x), and use IsSepClosed.lift to extend both embeddings. The algebra-hom commutes equations prove that both geometric points factor through the resulting point r: Spec K -> X.

Precomposition with each field embedding gives a natural transformation of the point fibre functors, with naturality given by associativity. Its components are bijections: Scheme.SpecMap_comp_injective gives injectivity, and the already proved Scheme.Hom.exists_SpecMap_comp_eq_of_isSepClosed in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFiniteRefinement.GeometricLifts gives surjectivity, including compatibility of the factored lift over X. This library lemma implements precisely the separable residue-field factorization in the planned step. Use isIso_iff_bijective and NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app to obtain the two fibre-functor isomorphisms.

Compose the inverse of the first fibre-functor isomorphism with the second, and apply Point.isoMk and Point.sheafFiberIso. For normalization prove the stronger elementary compatibility of any morphism of site points with the constant-stalk isomorphisms. Cancel the isomorphism induced by toSheafify, commute the point morphism with this map by naturality, and cancel its inverse in the explicit formula for sheafFiberConstantSheafIso. Apply presheafFiber_hom_ext: on each germ the induced point morphism merely changes the lift, while toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberConstIso_hom is identity on the constant value. Apply this compatibility to the inverse morphism of the constructed point isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_geometricStalkComparison_constant
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {Λ : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing Λ]
    [Limits.PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))]
    {Ω Ω' : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] [Field Ω'] [IsSepClosed Ω']
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (t : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ X)
    (h : s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω) = t (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω')) :
    ∃ β : (pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ≅
        (pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiber,
      ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ,
        β.hom.app ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M) ≫
          ((pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiberConstantSheafIso M).hom =
          ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiberConstantSheafIso M).hom
